newsitem.title: UK: Eurodollar supply shrugs off possible US rate rise.
newsitem.headline: Eurodollar supply shrugs off possible US rate rise.

text.p: Banks, companies and sovereign issuers have rushed to raise dollars in recent weeks on the strength of the currency and primary market syndicate managers have said a possible U.S. rate rise was unlikely to buck the trend.
"The first month is always a crazy time of year, issuers want to get a good start on their financing programmes," Merrill Lynch syndicate manager David Tory said.
"A lot of underwriters also feel compelled to be in the market right at the beginning," he added.
However an oversupply of Eurodollars from borrowers across the credit spectrum was a key concern, traders said.
"There is a lot of paper around and investors have a choice of maturities so some are sitting on their hands," CSFB syndicate manager Martin Egan said.

Eurodollar issuance accounted for 42 percent of the market share at $36 billion this January, versus $21 billion or 28 percent of market share for the same month last year, Capital DATA Bondware showed.

However, cautiousness ahead of next week's U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting will see a quieter period at the start of February following the hectic past weeks, which will give investors a chance to digest the new issues, traders said.
"Some concerns have come into the market regarding interest rates and there is now a strong focus on any U.S. economic data, but at the moment it all seems very controlled," Egan said.

Expectations are that FOMC chairman Alan Greenspan will hold off from raising key interest rates at the next meeting scheduled for February 4 and 5, but market players do not discount the risk of an increase entirely.
The U.S. federal funds rate, at 5.25 percent, was cut from 5.50 percent on January 31 last year. The discount rate, now at 5.0 percent, was last cut from 5.25 percent on the same date.
"Everyone expects interest rates to go up this year but nothing dramatic, only a slow gradual rise," Merrill Lynch syndicate manager David Tory said.

"The U.S. should lead Germany and Japan in interest rate rises which will mean the dollar will continue to rally and that is an important factor in determining whether investors will continue to support the sector," he added.
The dollar has climbed to new highs against the mark, yen and Swiss franc in recent weeks.
The mark was at 1.6365/72 against the dollar at 1500 GMT, while the yen was at 121.30/40 on the dollar. The mark started the year at around 1.54 on the dollar and the yen at around 115.
Large dollar redemptions also drove issuance at the start of the year. Redemptions of international bonds in January totalled $12.4 billion, according to Capital DATA Bondware.

"The reason we've seen the supply, particularly in the two - to four-year sector, is that the market has been in pretty good shape, the currency has been strong and there has been a heavy U.S. dollar redemption schedule," CSFB's Egan said.
Added to this, arbitrage opportunities in the dollar sector have been good.
